uslaw-usc-t2-s288f: Section 288f of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with court steps to grant a shield from a charge. It sits in Chapter 9D, on the Office of Senate Legal Counsel. When the Counsel is told to act under a named part of a past section, a duty falls on the Counsel. The Counsel is to act for the Senate, or for a panel of the Senate, in a court step. That step is a call on a district court for an order that grants the shield.
uslaw-usc-t2-s658f: Section 658f of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with calls by Senators for a count of costs. It sits in Chapter 17A, on the budget work of Congress, in a part on federal mandates. At the written call of a Senator, a duty falls on the Director of the Congressional Budget Office. The Director is, as far as can be done, to prep a count of the direct costs of a federal mandate. The mandate must be in a change put forth by that Senator.
